  "text": "The apartment upstairs had been empty for twelve years when someone began measuring the floor.

Every night at two, a tape measure rasped across the ceiling. Then came a pencil scratching, followed by three polite knocks.

My landlord stopped answering after I described the sound.

On Thursday, a folded diagram slid beneath my door.

It showed my bedroom from above: wardrobe, radiator, bed. A dotted line crossed my pillow.

In the margin someone had written: PLEASE MOVE SIX INCHES LEFT.

I slept on the sofa.

At two, something heavy struck the bedroom floor.

I found a narrow hole through my pillow, mattress, and the boards beneath. Its edges were perfectly smooth.

Another note waited outside.

THANK YOU FOR YOUR COOPERATION. SMALL ADJUSTMENT REQUIRED.

This diagram showed the sofa.

I went upstairs with a hammer.

The apartment door stood open. Inside, there were no rooms, only a wooden floor stretching farther than the building allowed.

A woman knelt beside a measuring tape.

She wore my mother's dressing gown.

My mother had been buried in it.

“Don't stand there,” she said without looking up.

I looked down.

Around my shoes, faint pencil marks formed a rectangle.

“What are you making?”

She pressed one finger to the floor. From beneath it came the sound of my television.

“Enough room.”

“For what?”

The tape measure snapped shut.

Across that enormous floor, thousands of pencil rectangles darkened. From under each came a different noise: running water, an argument, a baby crying.

My mother stood and reached for my hammer.

“Tomorrow we take out the walls.”"
